claim: Leber congenital amaurosis type nine is an autosomal recessive retinopathy caused by mutations of the NAD+ synthesis enzyme NMNAT1.
source: Leber congenital amaurosis type nine is an autosomal recessive retinopathy caused by mutations of the NAD+ synthesis enzyme NMNAT1.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and is supported by citations to prior literature in the introduction.

claim: LCA9 patients do not manifest pathologies other than retinal degeneration despite the ubiquitous expression of NMNAT1.
source: Despite the ubiquitous expression of NMNAT1, patients do not manifest pathologies other than retinal degeneration.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by clinical observations cited in the introduction.

claim: Widespread NMNAT1 depletion in adult mice mirrors the human pathology with selective loss of photoreceptors.
source: Here we demonstrate that widespread NMNAT1 depletion in adult mice mirrors the human pathology, with selective loss of photoreceptors highlighting the exquisite vulnerability of these cells to NMNAT1 loss.
evidence: This is demonstrated through experimental data using conditional knockout mice and histological analysis.

claim: NMNAT1 is required within the photoreceptor as demonstrated by conditional deletion.
source: Conditional deletion demonstrates that NMNAT1 is required within the photoreceptor.
evidence: This is supported by cell-type specific deletion experiments using Rho-Cre and OPN1LW-Cre mice.

claim: Loss of NMNAT1 activates the NADase SARM1 to trigger photoreceptor death and vision loss.
source: Mechanistically, loss of NMNAT1 activates the NADase SARM1, the central executioner of axon degeneration, to trigger photoreceptor death and vision loss.
evidence: This is demonstrated by metabolite analysis showing increased cADPR and rescue experiments in SARM1 knockout mice.

claim: The essential function of NMNAT1 in photoreceptors is to inhibit SARM1.
source: Hence, the essential function of NMNAT1 in photoreceptors is to inhibit SARM1, highlighting an unexpected shared mechanism between axonal degeneration and photoreceptor neurodegeneration.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue of photoreceptor degeneration in NMNAT1/SARM1 double knockout mice.

claim: SARM1 is a therapeutic candidate for retinopathies.
source: These results define a novel SARM1-dependent photoreceptor cell death pathway and identifies SARM1 as a therapeutic candidate for retinopathies.
evidence: This is speculated based on the finding that SARM1 deletion rescues photoreceptor degeneration.

claim: LCA is the most common cause of blindness in children.
source: LCA is the most common cause of blindness in children and about 70% of LCA cases are associated with mutations in genes related to the visual cycle, cGMP production, ciliogenesis, or transcription.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: More than thirty mutations in NMNAT1 were identified in patients with autosomal recessive LCA type 9.
source: Recently, more than thirty mutations in the nuclear NAD+ biosynthetic enzyme NMNAT1 were identified in patients with autosomal recessive LCA type 9 (LCA9) (Falk et al., 2012; Perrault et al., 2012; Koenekoop et al., 2012; Chiang et al., 2012; Coppieters et al., 2015; Khan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior studies.

claim: LCA9 patients have no other systemic deficits outside the retina.
source: Despite the ubiquitous expression of this key NAD+ biosynthesis enzyme, LCA9 patients have no other systemic deficits outside the retina.
evidence: This is stated as a clinical observation in the introduction.

claim: Many LCA9 associated mutant NMNAT1 proteins retain enzymatic activity but appear to be less stable under conditions associated with cell stress.
source: In many cases, LCA9 associated mutant NMNAT1 proteins retain enzymatic activity and other biochemical functions, but appear to be less stable under conditions associated with cell stress (Sasaki et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: NAD+ deficiency in the retina is an early feature of retinal degenerative disorders in mice.
source: While it is clear that NAD+ deficiency in the retina is an early feature of retinal degenerative disorders in mice (Zabka et al., 2015; Lin et al., 2016), it is not known which cell types and biological pathways are primarily affected in LCA9.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Overexpression of NMNAT1 in mouse retinal ganglion cells robustly protects against ischemic and glaucomatous loss of the axon and soma.
source: Overexpression of NMNAT1 in mouse retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) robustly protects against ischemic and glaucomatous loss of the axon and soma (Zhu et al., 2013), while conditional ablation in the developing mouse retina causes severe retinal dystrophy and loss of retinal function (Eblimit et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Conditional ablation of NMNAT1 in the developing mouse retina causes severe retinal dystrophy and loss of retinal function.
source: Overexpression of NMNAT1 in mouse retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) robustly protects against ischemic and glaucomatous loss of the axon and soma (Zhu et al., 2013), while conditional ablation in the developing mouse retina causes severe retinal dystrophy and loss of retinal function (Eblimit et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Mice harboring Nmnat1 mutations (V9M and D243G) exhibit severe retinal degeneration.
source: Mice harboring Nmnat1 mutations (V9M and D243G) exhibit severe retinal degeneration while the most common LCA9 mutation (E257K), which is not fully penetrant (Siemiatkowska et al., 2014), induces a milder retinal degeneration phenotype (Eblimit et al., 2018; Greenwald et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The most common LCA9 mutation (E257K) induces a milder retinal degeneration phenotype.
source: Mice harboring Nmnat1 mutations (V9M and D243G) exhibit severe retinal degeneration while the most common LCA9 mutation (E257K), which is not fully penetrant (Siemiatkowska et al., 2014), induces a milder retinal degeneration phenotype (Eblimit et al., 2018; Greenwald et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: NMNAT1 promotes the survival of mouse retinal progenitor cells in retinal explants.
source: In retinal explants, NMNAT1 promotes the survival of mouse retinal progenitor cells (Kuribayashi et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: The Drosophila NMNAT isoform, dNMNAT, is required for the survival of photoreceptor cells after exposure to intense light.
source: The requirement for NMNAT in retina is evolutionarily conserved, as the Drosophila NMNAT isoform, dNMNAT, is required for the survival of photoreceptor cells after exposure to intense light (Zhai et al., 2006; Zhai et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Variants in the NAD+ or NADPH dependent retinal dehydrogenase RDH12 cause LCA13.
source: These include variants in the NAD+ or NADPH dependent retinal dehydrogenases like RDH12 that cause LCA13 (Schuster et al., 2007) and the GTP synthesis enzyme IMPDH1 that causes retinitis pigmentosa (Kennan et al., 2002; Bowne et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: The GTP synthesis enzyme IMPDH1 causes retinitis pigmentosa.
source: These include variants in the NAD+ or NADPH dependent retinal dehydrogenases like RDH12 that cause LCA13 (Schuster et al., 2007) and the GTP synthesis enzyme IMPDH1 that causes retinitis pigmentosa (Kennan et al., 2002; Bowne et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: SIRT3, the mitochondrial NAD+-dependent deacetylase, is important for photoreceptor homeostasis.
source: SIRT3, the mitochondrial NAD+-dependent deacetylase is also important for photoreceptor homeostasis (Lin et al., 2016; Lin et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: NMNAT1 is the only NMNAT enzyme localized to the nucleus among the three mammalian NMNAT isoforms.
source: Among the three mammalian NMNAT isoforms, NMNAT1 is the only enzyme localized to the nucleus (Berger et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: In photoreceptors, NMNAT1 is present in photoreceptor outer segments.
source: However, in photoreceptors NMNAT1 is present in photoreceptor outer segments (Zhao et al., 2016), consistent with an additional, extra-nuclear role of NMNAT1 in photoreceptor cells.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Engineered non-nuclear variants of enzymatically-active NMNAT1 can potently inhibit pathological axon degeneration.
source: This is of particular interest because engineered non-nuclear variants of enzymatically-active NMNAT1 can potently inhibit pathological axon degeneration, which is commonly observed in the early stages of many neurodegenerative disorders (Walker et al., 2017; Sasaki et al., 2009; Babetto et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: When NMNAT1 is present in the axon, it can compensate for the injury-induced rapid loss of NMNAT2.
source: When NMNAT1 is present in the axon, it can compensate for the injury-induced rapid loss of NMNAT2, the endogenous axonal NMNAT (Gilley and Coleman, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: NMNAT2 inhibits SARM1, an inducible NAD+ cleavage enzyme that is the central executioner of axon degeneration.
source: NMNAT2 in turn, inhibits SARM1, an inducible NAD+ cleavage enzyme (NADase) that is the central executioner of axon degeneration (Gilley and Coleman, 2010; Gerdts et al., 2015; Sasaki et al., 2016; Gilley et al., 2015; Figley and DiAntonio, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Photoreceptors degenerate rapidly after the loss of NMNAT1 in conditional mutant mice.
source: Using NMNAT1 conditional mutant mice, we showed that photoreceptors degenerate rapidly after the loss of NMNAT1 and that depletion of NMNAT1 in rod or cone cells is necessary and sufficient for the retinal degeneration.
evidence: This is demonstrated through experimental data using conditional knockout mice.

claim: Depletion of NMNAT1 in rod or cone cells is necessary and sufficient for retinal degeneration.
source: Using NMNAT1 conditional mutant mice, we showed that photoreceptors degenerate rapidly after the loss of NMNAT1 and that depletion of NMNAT1 in rod or cone cells is necessary and sufficient for the retinal degeneration.
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell-type specific deletion experiments.

claim: AAV-mediated gene replacement of NMNAT1 in photoreceptors partially rescues the visual impairment caused by loss of NMNAT1.
source: The AAV-mediated gene replacement of NMNAT1 in photoreceptors partially rescues the visual impairment caused by loss of NMNAT1.
evidence: This is demonstrated through AAV gene therapy experiments and ERG measurements.

claim: Loss of NMNAT1 leads to activation of SARM1 in photoreceptors.
source: Loss of NMNAT1 leads to activation of SARM1 in photoreceptors, much as loss of NMNAT2 leads to SARM1 activation in axons (Gilley and Coleman, 2010).
evidence: This is demonstrated through metabolite analysis showing increased cADPR, a biomarker of SARM1 activity.

claim: Photoreceptor degeneration is mediated by SARM1 in the absence of NMNAT1.
source: Moreover, photoreceptor degeneration is mediated by SARM1 in the absence of NMNAT1, much as axon degeneration and perinatal lethality is mediated by SARM1 in the absence of NMNAT2 (Gilley and Coleman, 2010; Gilley et al., 2015).
evidence: This is demonstrated through rescue experiments in NMNAT1/SARM1 double knockout mice.

claim: The SARM1 pathway is likely druggable.
source: Since the SARM1 pathway is likely druggable (DiAntonio, 2019; Krauss et al., 2020), these findings provide a framework for developing new therapeutic strategies for treating patients with LCA9 and potentially other retinal disorders.
evidence: This is speculated based on citations to prior studies.

claim: NMNAT1 is indispensable for mouse development.
source: NMNAT1 is a nuclear enzyme that synthesizes NAD+, an essential metabolite that is central to all aspects of cellular metabolism. NMNAT1 is indispensable for mouse development (Conforti et al., 2011) and recent studies identified causative mutations in NMNAT1 in patients with Leber congenital amaurosis type 9 (LCA9), a disorder associated with severe, early-onset retinal degeneration and vision loss (Falk et al., 2012; Perrault et al., 2012; Koenekoop et al., 2012; Chiang et al., 2012; Coppieters et al., 2015; Khan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Certain cells within the retina are particularly vulnerable to the loss of NMNAT1 function.
source: Patients with LCA9 have no systemic involvement outside the eye, suggesting that certain cells within the retina are particularly vulnerable to the loss of NMNAT1 function.
evidence: This is inferred from the clinical observation that LCA9 patients have no systemic deficits.

claim: NMNAT1 expression is ubiquitous in the retina, including RPE, photoreceptor outer segments, inner segments, ONL, OPL, INL, IPL, and GCL.
source: LacZ staining was detected in the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), photoreceptor outer segments (OS), inner segments (IS), outer nuclear layer (ONL), outer plexiform layer (OPL), inner nuclear layer (INL), inner plexiform layer (IPL), and ganglion cell layer (GCL) suggesting the ubiquitous expression of NMNAT1 in retina (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through X-gal staining of retinal tissues from mice expressing NMNAT1-lacZ fusion protein.

claim: Nmnat1 mRNA is significantly decreased in NMNAT1 cKO retina at 21 days after tamoxifen compared with wild-type mice.
source: We first used RT-PCR to measure Nmnat1 mRNA in the retina at 21 days after tamoxifen and found that it was significantly decreased in NMNAT1 cKO (Nmnat1fl/fl: CAG-CreERT2 + tamoxifen) compared with wild-type (WT) mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative RT-PCR analysis.

claim: There is a significant increase in levels of NMN in NMNAT1 cKO retina at 25 days after tamoxifen injection.
source: There is a significant increase in levels of NMN, presumably because it cannot be consumed by NMNAT1.
evidence: This is demonstrated through metabolite analysis by LC-MSMS and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: There is a mild decrease in NAD+ in NMNAT1 cKO mice at 25 days after tamoxifen injection, although this is not statistically significant.
source: There is also a mild decrease in NAD+ in NMNAT1 cKO mice, although this is not statistically significant, suggesting that other NMNAT enzymes are an additional source of NAD+ (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through metabolite analysis by LC-MSMS.

claim: Other NMNAT enzymes are an additional source of NAD+ in NMNAT1 cKO mice.
source: There is also a mild decrease in NAD+ in NMNAT1 cKO mice, although this is not statistically significant, suggesting that other NMNAT enzymes are an additional source of NAD+ (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that NAD+ levels do not decrease significantly despite NMNAT1 deletion.

claim: Fundus images of NMNAT1 cKO mice at 4 weeks after Nmnat1 excision showed abnormalities including attenuation of blood vessels and the appearance of a honeycomb structure.
source: Fundus images showed abnormalities including attenuation of blood vessels (Figure 1C,D arrowhead) and the appearance of a honeycomb structure, suggesting exposure of retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells (Figure 1C,D arrow) in the mutant animals.
evidence: This is demonstrated through fundus biomicroscopy images.

claim: Histopathological examination of NMNAT1 cKO retina at 4 weeks post tamoxifen treatment showed severe retinal degeneration as evidenced by the reduction of the retina thickness and the thinning of the ONL.
source: Histopathological examination of the retina with hematoxylin and eosin (HE) stained sections showed severe retinal degeneration as evidenced by the reduction of the retina thickness and the thinning of the outer nuclear layer (ONL) at 4 weeks post tamoxifen treatment (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This is demonstrated through histological analysis of HE stained sections.

claim: Quantitative analysis demonstrated a significant reduction of retinal thickness, especially of the ONL, in NMNAT1 cKO mice.
source: Quantitative analysis demonstrated a significant reduction of retinal thickness, especially of the ONL (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of histological sections.

claim: Photoreceptor cells are highly vulnerable following the loss of NMNAT1.
source: Hence, photoreceptor cells are highly vulnerable following the loss of NMNAT1.
evidence: This is inferred from the selective loss of ONL cells in NMNAT1 cKO mice.

claim: The loss of nuclei in the ONL layers were evident at 25 days post tamoxifen injection in NMNAT1 cKO mice.
source: The loss of nuclei in the ONL layers were evident at 25 days post tamoxifen injection and robust retinal thinning was evident at 33 days post tamoxifen injection (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through histological analysis at multiple time points.

claim: Robust retinal thinning was evident at 33 days post tamoxifen injection in NMNAT1 cKO mice.
source: The loss of nuclei in the ONL layers were evident at 25 days post tamoxifen injection and robust retinal thinning was evident at 33 days post tamoxifen injection (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through histological analysis at multiple time points.

claim: Cell loss in the ONL was first detected around 3 weeks after tamoxifen administration and gradually progressed such that only ~15% of the cells remained at 33 days.
source: Cell loss was first detected in the ONL around 3 weeks after tamoxifen administration and gradually progressed such that only ~15% of the cells remained at 33 days (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of ONL nuclei counts.

claim: NMNAT1 cKO mice showed a complete loss of both scotopic (rod-driven responses) and photopic (cone-driven responses) responses at 33 days post tamoxifen treatment.
source: In mutant animals in which Nmnat1 was excised, we observed a complete loss of both scotopic (rod-driven responses) and photopic (cone-driven responses) responses, indicating the loss of Nmnat1 in mature retina causes severe photoreceptor dysfunction (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through ERG analysis.

claim: Loss of Nmnat1 in mature retina causes severe photoreceptor dysfunction.
source: In mutant animals in which Nmnat1 was excised, we observed a complete loss of both scotopic (rod-driven responses) and photopic (cone-driven responses) responses, indicating the loss of Nmnat1 in mature retina causes severe photoreceptor dysfunction (Figure 2C–E).
evidence: This is inferred from the complete loss of ERG responses.

claim: NMNAT1 is necessary for photoreceptor cell maintenance and mature retinal functions.
source: While previous reports show that Nmnat1 is necessary for appropriate retinal development, our pathological and functional analyses of conditional deletion of NMNAT1 in two-month-old mice demonstrates that NMNAT1 is also necessary for photoreceptor cell maintenance and mature retinal functions.
evidence: This is demonstrated through conditional deletion experiments in adult mice.

claim: NMNAT2 knockout mice are perinatally lethal and have truncated optic nerves as well as peripheral axon degeneration.
source: A previous study showed that NMNAT2 knockout mice are perinatally lethal and have truncated optic nerves as well as peripheral axon degeneration (Slivicki et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: NMNAT3 deficient mice are viable with splenomegaly and hemolytic anemia.
source: On the other hand, NMNAT3 deficient mice (NMNAT3 KO) are viable with splenomegaly and hemolytic anemia (Hikosaka et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: NMNAT3 KO mice showed no defects in ERG.
source: We generated NMNAT3 KO mice and investigated their retinal function using ERG. Consistent with the previous report, NMNAT3 KO mice showed splenomegaly (data not shown), however, there were no defects in ERG (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated through ERG analysis of NMNAT3 KO mice.

claim: NMNAT3 is dispensable for retinal function.
source: These results indicate that NMNAT3 is dispensable for retinal function, suggesting NMNAT1 is the functionally dominant isoform controlling retinal phenotype.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of ERG defects in NMNAT3 KO mice.

claim: NMNAT1 is the functionally dominant isoform controlling retinal phenotype.
source: These results indicate that NMNAT3 is dispensable for retinal function, suggesting NMNAT1 is the functionally dominant isoform controlling retinal phenotype.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of NMNAT1 and NMNAT3 knockout phenotypes.

claim: Histological analysis of Nmnat1fl/fl:Rho-Cre mice at 6-weeks-of-age revealed severe thinning of the ONL.
source: We analyzed the retinas of Nmnat1fl/fl:Rho-Cre mice at 6-weeks-of-age. Similar to previous findings using Crx-Cre that expresses Cre recombinase in developing photoreceptors as early as E11 (Eblimit et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2017), histological analysis revealed severe thinning of the ONL in these mutant mice (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through histological analysis of rod-specific NMNAT1 knockout mice.

claim: Quantitative analysis showed a significant reduction of the retina and ONL thickness in Nmnat1fl/fl:Rho-Cre retina.
source: The quantitative analysis showed a significant reduction of the retina and ONL thickness in Nmnat1fl/fl:Rho-Cre retina (Figure 3D) as well as a significant reduction in ONL cell number as detected by nuclear counts (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of histological sections.

claim: ERG analysis showed a severe reduction in the scotopic a- and b-waves in the Nmnat1fl/fl:Rho-Cre mice.
source: Consistent with the loss of ONL cells, ERG analysis showed a severe reduction in the scotopic a- and –b-waves, representing rod photoreceptor function, in the Nmnat1fl/fl:Rho-Cre mice (Figure 3G,H).
evidence: This is demonstrated through ERG analysis of rod-specific NMNAT1 knockout mice.

claim: Nmnat1fl/fl:Rho-Cre mice showed decreases in cone mediated photoresponses (photopic b-wave signal) that is likely secondary to a loss of rod photoreceptor cells.
source: In addition, we found decreases in cone mediated photoresponses (photopic b-wave signal) (Figure 3I) that is likely secondary to a loss of rod photoreceptor cells due to loss of required rod-derived survival factors (Lin et al., 2016; Aït-Ali et al., 2015).
evidence: This is demonstrated through ERG analysis and inferred from prior studies on rod-derived survival factors.

claim: ERG analysis of Nmnat1fl/fl:OPN1LW-Cre mice at 6-weeks-of-age showed a complete loss of the photopic b-wave.
source: However, ERG analysis showed a complete loss of the photopic b-wave, which is derived from cone photoreceptors. This functional result demonstrates that NMNAT1 activity is vital for cone function (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is demonstrated through ERG analysis of cone-specific NMNAT1 knockout mice.

claim: NMNAT1 activity is vital for cone function.
source: However, ERG analysis showed a complete loss of the photopic b-wave, which is derived from cone photoreceptors. This functional result demonstrates that NMNAT1 activity is vital for cone function (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is inferred from the complete loss of photopic b-wave in cone-specific NMNAT1 knockout mice.

claim: LCA9-associated retinal degeneration is likely due to the direct cell-autonomous effects of NMNAT1 mutations in photoreceptors.
source: In summary, these genetic ablation experiments demonstrate the importance of NMNAT1 for proper function and survival of both rods and cones, and indicate that LCA9-associated retinal degeneration is likely due to the direct cell-autonomous effects of NMNAT1 mutations in photoreceptors.
evidence: This is inferred from the cell-type specific deletion experiments.

claim: AAV8(Y733F) containing the photoreceptor-specific human rhodopsin kinase (hGRK1) promoter driving GFP shows transgene expression in a subset of rhodopsin-positive cells but is weak in the inner nuclear layer.
source: AAV-mediated GFP expression was observed in a subset of rhodopsin-positive cells but was weak in the inner nuclear layer (INL) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through fluorescent microscopy of AAV-transduced retinas.

claim: The hGRK1 promoter restricts transgene expression primarily to photoreceptors.
source: These results confirm earlier reports that the hGRK1 promoter restricts transgene expression primarily to photoreceptors (Kay et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and a citation to a prior study.

claim: AAV-NMNAT1 treated retinas showed significantly increased scotopic a-wave amplitudes compared with retinas injected with AAV-GFP.
source: Despite the expression of NMNAT1 in only a subset of photoreceptors, we observed significantly increased scotopic a-wave amplitudes in AAV-NMNAT1 treated retinas compared with retinas injected with AAV-GFP (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D; Figure 3D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through ERG analysis of AAV-treated mice.

claim: There were small, but statistically insignificant, increases in the scotopic and photopic b-wave amplitudes between AAV-NMNAT1 and AAV-GFP treated retinas.
source: There were also small, but statistically insignificant, increases in the scotopic and photopic b-wave amplitudes between AAV-NMNAT1 and AAV-GFP treated retinas (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is demonstrated through ERG analysis of AAV-treated mice.

claim: NMNAT1 gene delivery to photoreceptor cells significantly improved their function in this LCA9 model.
source: Hence, NMNAT1 gene delivery to photoreceptor cells significantly improved their function in this LCA9 model.
evidence: This is inferred from the ERG improvements in AAV-NMNAT1 treated mice.

claim: In injured peripheral nerves, the loss of NMNAT2 induces an increase in NMN that is hypothesized to activate SARM1-dependent axon degeneration.
source: In injured peripheral nerves, the loss of NMNAT2 induces an increase in NMN that is hypothesized to activate SARM1-dependent axon degeneration (Di Stefano et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: NMN is increased in the NMNAT1-deficient retinas.
source: Our metabolomic analysis revealed that NMN is increased in the NMNAT1-deficient retinas (Figure 1B), and previous studies have detected SARM1 in mouse and bovine photoreceptor cells (Zhao et al., 2016; Datta et al., 2015; Menon et al., 2019).
evidence: This is demonstrated through metabolite analysis.

claim: SARM1 has been detected in mouse and bovine photoreceptor cells.
source: Our metabolomic analysis revealed that NMN is increased in the NMNAT1-deficient retinas (Figure 1B), and previous studies have detected SARM1 in mouse and bovine photoreceptor cells (Zhao et al., 2016; Datta et al., 2015; Menon et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: There was significant loss of NAD+ at 29 to 32 days post tamoxifen in NMNAT1 cKO but not in NMNAT1 cKO: SARM1 KO retina.
source: While the loss of NAD+ was not statistically significant at 25 days post tamoxifen injection in NMNAT1 cKO retina (Figure 1A), there was significant loss of NAD+ at 29 to 32 days post tamoxifen in NMNAT1 cKO but not in NMNAT1 cKO: SARM1 KO retina (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through metabolite analysis by LC-MSMS.

claim: There was a significant increase of cADPR in NMNAT1 cKO retina in a SARM1-dependent manner.
source: Consistent with this idea, we also observed a significant increase of cADPR in NMNAT1 cKO retina in a SARM1-dependent manner (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through metabolite analysis by LC-MSMS.

claim: SARM1 is activated by the loss of NMNAT1.
source: Hence, SARM1 is activated by the loss of NMNAT1.
evidence: This is inferred from the increase in cADPR, a biomarker of SARM1 activity.

claim: There was no obvious loss of ONL cells in NMNAT1 cKO: SARM1 KO retina at 32 days post tamoxifen injection.
source: While there is a dramatic loss of ONL nuclei 32 days post tamoxifen injection in NMNAT1 cKO retina, there was no obvious loss of ONL cells in NMNAT1 cKO: SARM1 KO retina (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through histological analysis.

claim: Quantitative analysis showed no reduction of retinal and ONL thickness in NMNAT1 cKO:SARM1 KO retina compared with WT.
source: Quantitative analysis showed no reduction of retinal and ONL thickness in NMNAT1 cKO:SARM1 KO retina compared with WT (Figure 4F,G) in sharp contrast to the dramatic loss of retinal and ONL thickness in the NMNAT1 cKO (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of histological sections.

claim: There was no detectable loss of ONL nuclei in NMNAT1 cKO:SARM1 KO compared with WT.
source: Moreover, there was no detectable loss of ONL nuclei in NMNAT1 cKO:SARM1 KO compared with WT, demonstrating that SARM1 is necessary for photoreceptor cell death induced by the loss of NMNAT1 (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is demonstrated through quantitative analysis of ONL nuclei counts.

claim: SARM1 is necessary for photoreceptor cell death induced by the loss of NMNAT1.
source: Moreover, there was no detectable loss of ONL nuclei in NMNAT1 cKO:SARM1 KO compared with WT, demonstrating that SARM1 is necessary for photoreceptor cell death induced by the loss of NMNAT1 (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue of photoreceptor loss in NMNAT1/SARM1 double knockout mice.

claim: Loss of SARM1 prevented the severe loss of both scotopic and photopic responses due to NMNAT1 deficiency.
source: We next examined the functional consequences of NMNAT1 depletion in the presence or absence of SARM1 using ERGs, and again found that loss of SARM1 prevented the severe loss of both scotopic and photopic responses due to NMNAT1 deficiency (Figure 4I–K).
evidence: This is demonstrated through ERG analysis of NMNAT1/SARM1 double knockout mice.

claim: Loss of NMNAT1 leads to the activation of SARM1, and SARM1 is required for the subsequent photoreceptor degeneration and loss of visual function.
source: Taken together, these findings demonstrate that loss of NMNAT1 leads to the activation of SARM1, and that SARM1 is required for the subsequent photoreceptor degeneration and loss of visual function.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined metabolite and rescue experiments.

claim: Inhibition of SARM1 is a candidate therapeutic strategy for the treatment of LCA9.
source: Therefore, the essential function of NMNAT1 in photoreceptors is to inhibit SARM1, and inhibition of SARM1 is a candidate therapeutic strategy for the treatment of LCA9.
evidence: This is speculated based on the rescue of photoreceptor degeneration in SARM1 knockout mice.

claim: Deletion of NMNAT1 in the adult retina causes a dramatic loss of photoreceptors and a concomitant reduction in retinal function.
source: In this study, we demonstrate that deletion of NMNAT1 in the adult retina causes a dramatic loss of photoreceptors and a concomitant reduction in retinal function.
evidence: This is demonstrated through conditional deletion experiments in adult mice.

claim: Cell-type specific deletion of NMNAT1 in early postnatal photoreceptors is sufficient to induce retinal degeneration.
source: In addition, cell-type specific deletion of NMNAT1 in early postnatal photoreceptors is sufficient to induce retinal degeneration.
evidence: This is demonstrated through rod- and cone-specific deletion experiments.

claim: NMNAT1 is required for the survival and function of both developing and mature photoreceptors.
source: Hence, NMNAT1 is required for the survival and function of both developing and mature photoreceptors.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined results of developmental and adult deletion experiments.

claim: A gene replacement strategy using modified AAV8 vector and the human rhodopsin kinase promoter to express NMNAT1 can improve retinal function in this model of LCA9.
source: Using a modified AAV8 vector and the human rhodopsin kinase promoter to express NMNAT1, we demonstrated that a gene replacement strategy can improve retinal function in this model of LCA9.
evidence: This is demonstrated through AAV gene therapy experiments.

claim: Loss of NMNAT1 in photoreceptors or NMNAT2 in axons leads to the SARM1-induced death of photoreceptors or axons, respectively.
source: Loss of NMNAT1 in photoreceptors or NMNAT2 in axons leads to the SARM1-induced death of photoreceptors or axons, respectively.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of photoreceptor and axon degeneration mechanisms.

claim: This finding defines a common mechanism operant in both photoreceptor degeneration and pathological axon degeneration.
source: This finding defines a common mechanism operant in both photoreceptor degeneration and pathological axon degeneration.
evidence: This is inferred from the shared SARM1-dependent mechanism.

claim: This result extends our understanding of both the mechanisms causing retinal degeneration and the potential role of SARM1 in human disease.
source: This surprising result extends our understanding of both the mechanisms causing retinal degeneration and the potential role of SARM1 in human disease (Figley and DiAntonio, 2020; Coleman and Höke, 2020).
evidence: This is speculated based on the findings and supported by citations.

claim: Reduced NAD+ induces mitochondrial dysfunction in photoreceptor cells and affects activity of SIRT3.
source: Reduced NAD+ induces mitochondrial dysfunction in photoreceptor cells and affects activity of SIRT3, which protects the retina from light-induced and other forms of neurodegeneration.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: Combined deletion of retinal dehydrogenases, RDH12 and RDH8, results in mouse retinal degeneration.
source: For example, mutations in all-trans-retinal dehydrogenase (RDH12) that is localized to photoreceptor cells are associated with LCA13. Combined deletion of retinal dehydrogenases, RDH12 and RDH8, results in mouse retinal degeneration (Maeda et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: IMPDH1 mutations cause both a dominant form of retinitis pigmentosa (RP10) and LCA11.
source: IMPDH1 mutations cause both a dominant form of retinitis pigmentosa (RP10) and LCA11.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: A subcellular proteomics study showed the existence and enrichment of NMNAT1 in the photoreceptor outer segments.
source: In photoreceptors NMNAT1 may localize not only in the nucleus but also outside the nucleus, since a subcellular proteomics study showed the existence and enrichment of NMNAT1 in the photoreceptor outer segments (Zhao et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: Single-cell transcriptomic RNA analysis found Nmnat1 in rods and cones.
source: Single-cell transcriptomic RNA analysis also found Nmnat1 in rods and cones (Menon et al., 2019; Lukowski et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: In single-cell transcriptomic studies, cytosolic NMNAT2 was either not identified or was found at much lower levels than NMNAT1 in photoreceptors.
source: Consistent with an extranuclear role for NMNAT1 in photoreceptors, in these studies cytosolic NMNAT2 was either not identified or was found at much lower levels than NMNAT1.
evidence: This is inferred from single-cell transcriptomic data.

claim: The U.S. FDA approved an AAV-RPE65 vector as a therapeutic reagent for LCA2 and other biallelic RPE65 mutation associated retinal dystrophies.
source: Recently, the U.S. FDA approved an AAV-RPE65 vector as a therapeutic reagent for LCA2 and other biallelic RPE65 mutation associated retinal dystrophies (Apte, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation.

claim: LCA9 caused by the loss of NMNAT1 function is a reasonable target for AAV-mediated gene therapy.
source: Theoretically, LCA9 caused by the loss of NMNAT1 function is a reasonable target for AAV-mediated gene therapy.
evidence: This is speculated based on the success of AAV gene therapy for other LCA types.

claim: Delivery of AAV8(Y733F)-hGRK1-NMNAT1 prior to deletion of NMNAT1 resulted in partial improvement of the retinal phenotype, in particular the scotopic a-wave.
source: Delivery of AAV8(Y733F)-hGRK1-NMNAT1 prior to deletion of NMNAT1 resulted in partial improvement of the retinal phenotype, in particular the scotopic a-wave, of mice deficient for NMNAT1.
evidence: This is demonstrated through AAV gene therapy experiments.

claim: When NMNAT1 is deleted from SARM1 KO photoreceptors, the photoreceptors do not die and maintain their physiological function.
source: When NMNAT1 is deleted from SARM1 KO photoreceptors, the photoreceptors do not die and but instead maintain their physiological function, demonstrating that these cells do not require NMNAT1 as long as SARM1 is not present.
evidence: This is demonstrated through NMNAT1/SARM1 double knockout experiments.

claim: Photoreceptors do not require NMNAT1 as long as SARM1 is not present.
source: When NMNAT1 is deleted from SARM1 KO photoreceptors, the photoreceptors do not die and but instead maintain their physiological function, demonstrating that these cells do not require NMNAT1 as long as SARM1 is not present.
evidence: This is inferred from the rescue of photoreceptors in NMNAT1/SARM1 double knockout mice.

claim: The relationship between NMNAT1 and SARM1 in photoreceptors is analogous to the relationship between NMNAT2 and SARM1 in the axon.
source: This finding is perfectly analogous to the relationship between NMNAT2 and SARM1 in the axon.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of the two systems.

claim: NMNAT2 KO mice are perinatal lethal and have dramatic axonal defects, but NMNAT2, SARM1 double KO mice are viable and have a normal lifespan.
source: NMNAT2 KO mice are perinatal lethal and have dramatic axonal defects, but NMNAT2, SARM1 double KO mice are viable and have a normal lifespan (Gilley et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: NMNAT enzymes inhibit the activation of SARM1.
source: NMNAT enzymes inhibit the activation of SARM1 (Sasaki et al., 2016), potentially by consuming the NAD+ precursor NMN, which is postulated to activate SARM1 (Di Stefano et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: NMN is postulated to activate SARM1.
source: NMNAT enzymes inhibit the activation of SARM1 (Sasaki et al., 2016), potentially by consuming the NAD+ precursor NMN, which is postulated to activate SARM1 (Di Stefano et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Loss of NMNAT2 was the only known trigger of SARM1 activation prior to this study.
source: Prior to our current study, loss of NMNAT2 was the only known trigger of SARM1 activation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: SARM1 is activated by the loss of any NMNAT enzyme whose activity is not redundant with another NMNAT isoform.
source: Our current work suggests that SARM1 is activated by the loss of any NMNAT enzyme whose activity is not redundant with another NMNAT isoform.
evidence: This is inferred from the findings in both axons and photoreceptors.

claim: NMNAT2 is the only cytosolic NMNAT in the axon.
source: NMNAT2 is the only cytosolic NMNAT in the axon, and so loss of axonal NMNAT2 leads to localized activation of SARM1 and axon degeneration.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Loss of axonal NMNAT2 leads to localized activation of SARM1 and axon degeneration.
source: NMNAT2 is the only cytosolic NMNAT in the axon, and so loss of axonal NMNAT2 leads to localized activation of SARM1 and axon degeneration.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: In photoreceptors, NMNAT1 is not only nuclear but also likely extranuclear, and NMNAT2 is apparently present at very low levels.
source: In photoreceptors, NMNAT1 is not only nuclear but also likely extranuclear, and NMNAT2 is apparently present at very low levels.
evidence: This is inferred from proteomics and transcriptomic data.

claim: In photoreceptors, loss of NMNAT1 triggers activation of SARM1 which consumes NAD+ and triggers cell death.
source: Hence, in photoreceptors loss of NMNAT1 triggers activation of SARM1 which consumes NAD+ and triggers cell death.
evidence: This is inferred from the metabolite and rescue experiments.

claim: NAD+ loss is a common pathology of many retinal diseases.
source: As NAD+ loss is a common pathology of many retinal diseases, this raises the possibility that SARM1 activation may contribute to a wide range of retinal disorders.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: SARM1 activation may contribute to a wide range of retinal disorders.
source: As NAD+ loss is a common pathology of many retinal diseases, this raises the possibility that SARM1 activation may contribute to a wide range of retinal disorders.
evidence: This is speculated based on the findings.

claim: SARM1 promotes retinal degeneration in X-linked retinoschisis.
source: In support of this conjecture, recent studies found that SARM1 promotes retinal degeneration in X-linked retinoschisis (Molday et al., 2007) and rhodopsin-deficient mice (Ozaki et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: SARM1 promotes retinal degeneration in rhodopsin-deficient mice.
source: In support of this conjecture, recent studies found that SARM1 promotes retinal degeneration in X-linked retinoschisis (Molday et al., 2007) and rhodopsin-deficient mice (Ozaki et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: AAV-mediated expression of dominant negative SARM1 strongly protects injured axons from degeneration in the peripheral nervous system.
source: We previously developed a potent dominant negative SARM1 variant and demonstrated that AAV-mediated expression of dominant negative SARM1 strongly protects injured axons from degeneration in the peripheral nervous system (Geisler et al., 2019) and is also effective in a neuroinflammatory model of glaucoma (Ko et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: AAV-mediated expression of dominant negative SARM1 is effective in a neuroinflammatory model of glaucoma.
source: We previously developed a potent dominant negative SARM1 variant and demonstrated that AAV-mediated expression of dominant negative SARM1 strongly protects injured axons from degeneration in the peripheral nervous system (Geisler et al., 2019) and is also effective in a neuroinflammatory model of glaucoma (Ko et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study.

claim: If SARM1 plays a more general role in retinal degeneration, then using gene therapy to express dominant negative SARM1 could treat LCA9 and multiple retinal neurodegenerative diseases.
source: While NMNAT1 gene replacement is a potential treatment option for LCA9, if SARM1 plays a more general role in retinal degeneration, then using gene therapy to express this dominant negative SARM1 could not only treat LCA9, but also multiple retinal neurodegenerative diseases.
evidence: This is speculated based on the findings.

claim: SARM1 is an enzyme and so small molecule enzyme inhibitors would be an attractive treatment modality.
source: In addition, SARM1 is an enzyme and so small molecule enzyme inhibitors would be another attractive treatment modality (DiAntonio, 2019; Krauss et al., 2020).
evidence: This is speculated based on the nature of SARM1 and supported by citations.

claim: These findings demonstrate the utility of dissecting the molecular mechanism of degeneration in diseases of retinal neurodegeneration.
source: These findings demonstrate the utility of dissecting the molecular mechanism of degeneration in diseases of retinal neurodegeneration.
evidence: This is inferred from the overall findings of the study.

claim: These studies identified a SARM1-dependent photoreceptor cell death pathway.
source: In the case of LCA9, these studies identified a SARM1-dependent photoreceptor cell death pathway and discovered the heretofore unknown commonality between the mechanism of retinal neurodegeneration and pathological axon degeneration.
evidence: This is demonstrated through the experimental findings.

claim: These studies discovered the heretofore unknown commonality between the mechanism of retinal neurodegeneration and pathological axon degeneration.
source: In the case of LCA9, these studies identified a SARM1-dependent photoreceptor cell death pathway and discovered the heretofore unknown commonality between the mechanism of retinal neurodegeneration and pathological axon degeneration.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of the two degenerative mechanisms.
